step1_summary: Chief complaint: 2 months of significant anxiety, worsened by new, stressful job; morning dread of leaving the house; palpitations.

Symptoms: Onset ~2 months ago, coinciding with starting a new job; anxiety focused on work and public transport; insomnia (sleep latency hours, total 3–4 h/night), early morning awakening with racing heart; daytime low energy; anhedonia; social withdrawal/avoidance; constant worry; no clear panic attacks; palpitations described as fast and irregular, lasting minutes up to ~10 min; no typical chest pain (only discomfort when heart races).
Severity/aggravating/alleviating: Worse in mornings and with work-related stress; triggered by fear of being late; tube travel is stressful; persists on weekends to a lesser extent.
Past medical history: No prior similar episodes; no stated chronic medical conditions. No prior therapy; mother has history of depression.
Medications/allergies: None mentioned; no known drug use; not on psychiatric meds.

Family/social history: Lives with parents; supportive family; mother with depression. Alcohol: binge drinking most weekends (exceeds limits), plus occasional glasses during the week; occasional smoking; no illicit drugs.
Mental health risk: Denies suicidal ideation or intent; wants help, good support system.
Labs/imaging: None yet; GP plans basic blood tests (likely thyroid function, FBC, etc.).

V: Paroxysmal arrhythmia (e.g., SVT, AF, frequent PACs): Irregular, rapid palpitations lasting minutes, perceived as racing and distressing; anxiety may both trigger and amplify awareness.
I: Thyroiditis (subacute or painless) causing transient hyperthyroidism: Can cause palpitations, anxiety, sleep disturbance; would be screened via thyroid function tests.
N: Pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma: Episodic catecholamine surges can cause palpitations and anxiety, but rare and no headaches/diaphoresis/hypertension documented.
D: Iron-deficiency anemia: Can cause palpitations, fatigue, low energy; to be assessed with FBC/iron studies.
Vitamin B12/folate deficiency: Can contribute to fatigue/low mood.
I2: Substance-related anxiety/palpitations (alcohol, nicotine, caffeine): Weekend binge drinking and occasional smoking can worsen sleep, anxiety, and palpitations, especially mornings after use.
C: Congenital accessory pathway (e.g., WPW) with SVT: Less likely without prior history, but congenital arrhythmias can present with episodic palpitations in young adults.
A: Graves’ disease (autoimmune hyperthyroidism): Anxiety, palpitations, insomnia; to be evaluated with TSH/free T4.
T: Psychological stressor/occupational stress leading to adjustment disorder: Clear temporal link to starting a new, highly stressful job with perceived bullying/supervisor conflicts.
E: Generalized anxiety disorder (early course): Excessive worry across domains, restlessness, sleep disturbance; duration <6 months but symptom pattern fits.
Major depressive episode with anxious distress: Anhedonia, low mood, insomnia, fatigue for >2 weeks with prominent anxiety.
Hyperthyroidism: Endocrine cause of anxiety, palpitations, insomnia; to be ruled out.

step3_ranked_ddx.diagnosis: Adjustment disorder with mixed anxiety and depressed mood (work-related)
step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Symptoms began within ~2 months of a clear psychosocial stressor (new, highly stressful job). Prominent anxiety, insomnia, functional impairment, and depressive symptoms without prior history, fitting adjustment disorder timing and context.

Excessive worry most days, insomnia, restlessness, muscle tension-like symptoms (palpitations), functional impairment. Duration is 2 months (short of 6-month DSM threshold) but clinical picture is consistent and may evolve into GAD.

step3_ranked_ddx.diagnosis: Major depressive episode with anxious distress
step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Depressed mood, anhedonia, insomnia, fatigue, and social withdrawal for >2 weeks, with significant anxious distress; no suicidality. Anxiety may be comorbid or a specifier.
Palpitations, anxiety, and insomnia could be endocrine-driven; absence of weight loss, heat intolerance, tremor, or goiter makes it less likely, but standard to rule out.

step3_ranked_ddx.diagnosis: Paroxysmal arrhythmia (SVT/AF or ectopy) causing palpitations
step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Patient perceives irregular, rapid heartbeats lasting minutes. Young age and clear anxiety trigger suggest sinus tachycardia or ectopy; still consider ambulatory monitoring if persistent or atypical.

step4_supporting_opposing.diagnosis: Adjustment disorder with mixed anxiety and depressed mood (work-related)
supporting_evidence: Onset within 2 months of a major stressor (new, stressful job; difficult boss).
Prominent anxiety focused on work and commuting; functional impact (dread of leaving house, impaired sleep, avoidance of activities).
Concurrent low mood and anhedonia; no prior similar episodes.
opposing_evidence: Symptoms also present on weekends to some degree, suggesting broader generalization (though still related to ongoing stressor).

supporting_evidence: Excessive worry most days, difficulty controlling worry.
Physical symptoms: palpitations, restlessness, sleep disturbance, fatigue.
Impairment in social and occupational functioning.
opposing_evidence: Worry predominantly centered on a specific stressor (work), favoring adjustment disorder.

step4_supporting_opposing.diagnosis: Major depressive episode with anxious distress
supporting_evidence: Low mood most days, anhedonia, fatigue, insomnia, social withdrawal.
opposing_evidence: Anxiety appears primary with clear external trigger.
Denies suicidality; appetite largely unchanged; no psychomotor changes reported.

supporting_evidence: Palpitations, anxiety, insomnia are classic features.
Standard to exclude in new-onset anxiety with palpitations.
opposing_evidence: No weight loss, heat intolerance, tremor, diarrhea, or goiter reported.
Clear psychosocial trigger aligns more with primary anxiety/depressive disorders.

step4_supporting_opposing.diagnosis: Paroxysmal arrhythmia (SVT/AF or ectopy) causing palpitations
supporting_evidence: Subjective description of irregular, fast palpitations lasting minutes to ~10 minutes.
opposing_evidence: No syncope, presyncope, significant chest pain, or dyspnea.
Temporal link to anxiety and morning stress; young patient without cardiac history.
Palpitations often occur with anticipatory anxiety about being late.
